title: Adjoint local model maps embed into a product under joint zero detection
statement: Let $\mathcal A$ and $(\mathcal B_i)_{i\in I}$ be abelian categories [def-sp-abelian], with $I$ a set. For each $i$ let $F_i:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B_i$ be an additive functor [def-weil-pbc-additive-functor] preserving kernels, and let $G_i:\mathcal B_i\to\mathcal A$ be a right adjoint, with adjunction unit $\eta_i:\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal A}\to G_iF_i$. Here $F_i\dashv G_i$ means specified natural bijections $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal B_i}(F_iM,B)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal A}(M,G_iB)$, with their unit and counit. Suppose the $F_i$ jointly detect zero objects: if $F_iN$ is zero for every $i$, then $N$ is zero. Fix $M\in\mathcal A$, objects $B_i\in\mathcal B_i$, and isomorphisms $e_i:F_iM\xrightarrow{\sim}B_i$. If the product $P=\prod_{i\in I}G_iB_i$ exists [def-weil-category-product], the map $u:M\to P$ whose $i$-th component is $G_i(e_i)\circ\eta_{i,M}$ is a monomorphism. In particular this applies to $B_i=F_iM$ and $e_i=\mathrm{id}$.

source.place: Essentially small paragraph, global gluing from stratum restrictions; categorical kernel-and-adjunction argument isolated from retained original step 6

proof.text: Write $u_i=G_i(e_i)\circ\eta_{i,M}$ and let $p_i:P\to G_iB_i$ be the product projections, so $p_i\circ u=u_i$ by [def-weil-category-product]. Since $\mathcal A$ is abelian [def-sp-abelian], choose a kernel $k:K\to M$ of $u$: $u\circ k=0$, and every $h:T\to M$ with $u\circ h=0$ factors uniquely as $k\circ t$. Then $u_i\circ k=p_i\circ u\circ k=0$ for every $i$. These are only the product and kernel defining equations; no product preservation is asserted.

source.place: Tag 0106 (definition-kernel); product definition Tag 002I in categories.tex; blueprint Essentially small paragraph, global gluing

proof.text: Fix $i$. Additivity [def-weil-pbc-additive-functor] gives $F_i(0_{K,M})=0$. Let $\Phi_{N,B}:\operatorname{Hom}(F_iN,B)\to\operatorname{Hom}(N,G_iB)$ be the specified adjunction bijection; its naturality and definition of the unit give $\Phi_{M,B_i}(e_i)=u_i$. Naturality in $N$ at $k$ and at $0_{K,M}$ gives respectively $\Phi_{K,B_i}(e_i\circ F_i(k))=u_i\circ k=0$ and $\Phi_{K,B_i}(e_i\circ F_i(0_{K,M}))=u_i\circ0=0$. Injectivity of $\Phi_{K,B_i}$ therefore gives $e_i\circ F_i(k)=e_i\circ F_i(0_{K,M})=0$. Compose with $e_i^{-1}$ to obtain $F_i(k)=0$. Zero composites here follow from bilinearity [def-weil-preadditive-category].

source.place: Tag 0037 (definition-adjoint), naturality and paragraph defining unit; Tag 00ZY (definition-preadditive) in homology.tex

proof.text: By the assumed preservation of kernels, $F_i(k):F_iK\to F_iM$ is a kernel of $F_i(u)$. Its defining uniqueness, applied to the zero arrow $F_iK\to F_iM$, identifies the two factorizations $\mathrm{id}_{F_iK}$ and $0_{F_iK,F_iK}$, because $F_i(k)=0$. Thus $\mathrm{id}_{F_iK}=0$. Every arrow into $F_iK$ is zero by composing with this identity, and every arrow out of $F_iK$ is zero for the same reason; zero arrows exist and composition is bilinear [def-weil-preadditive-category]. Hence $F_iK$ is both initial and terminal, that is, a zero object. This proves the required assertion for each $i$ directly from the kernel universal property.

source.place: Tags 0106 (definition-kernel) and 00ZY (definition-preadditive): uniqueness of kernel factorization and bilinearity

proof.text: The joint zero-detection hypothesis now applies to the single object $K$, since the preceding step proved that $F_iK$ is zero for every $i$. Thus $K$ is a zero object. Its endomorphisms $\mathrm{id}_K$ and $0_{K,K}$ coincide by uniqueness, and consequently $k=k\circ\mathrm{id}_K=k\circ0=0$, using bilinearity [def-weil-preadditive-category].

source.place: Essentially small paragraph, adjunction-unit embedding: apply the joint zero-detection assumption to its kernel

proof.text: For any object $T$ and arrows $a,b:T\to M$ satisfying $u\circ a=u\circ b$, bilinearity [def-weil-preadditive-category] gives $u\circ(a-b)=0$. The kernel property from step 1 supplies $t:T\to K$ with $a-b=k\circ t$. Since $k=0$, this says $a-b=0$ and hence $a=b$. This is precisely the cancellation definition of $u$ being a monomorphism. Thus no separate zero-kernel criterion or exactness theorem is being invoked.

source.place: Tags 0106 (definition-kernel) and 00ZY (definition-preadditive): kernel factorization of a difference

proof.text: For the final assertion take $B_i=F_iM$ and $e_i=\mathrm{id}_{F_iM}$. These are isomorphisms, and functoriality gives $G_i(e_i)\circ\eta_{i,M}=\eta_{i,M}$. The result just proved therefore states that the map with the adjunction units as its components is monic whenever its product exists.
